einzeiler: How to build wealth for your children through smart accounts and business strategies.
kurzfassung: The host explains the specific financial steps she takes to build wealth for her toddler daughter. She details how to utilize accounts like a 529 plan, a custodial brokerage, and a custodial Roth IRA by employing children in a family business. Additionally, she compares term and whole life insurance policies to determine the best option for protecting a child's financial future.
stichpunkte: Setting up three specific financial accounts for a child: a 529 plan, a custodial brokerage, and a custodial Roth IRA
Sharing a 529 gift link with friends and family for holidays to collect direct contributions
Employing a child in a business for legitimate tasks like social media modeling to fund a Roth IRA legally
Paying a child up to the standard deduction limit, which is $16,100 for single filers in 2026
Maximizing tax advantages by utilizing a Roth IRA for tax-free withdrawals in retirement
Comparing term life insurance and whole life insurance to choose the most cost-effective coverage option
Opting for a 20-year term life insurance policy and investing the difference into market accounts
Front-loading a 529 plan by packing five years of contributions into a single year without triggering gift taxes

clips.text: A guest visiting the studio experienced an unexpected greeting when the toddler walked over and licked multiple water glasses.
The new standard deduction allows children to be paid up to $16,100 without needing to file a federal tax return.

clips.hook: Growing a million dollars for a child
clips.text: Starting early with a $7,000 contribution can grow into over a million dollars by the time the child reaches age sixty without any extra additions.

clips.hook: Why term life insurance beats whole life
clips.text: Choosing to invest the price difference directly into the market yields better results than paying for expensive whole life insurance products.
The IRS permits individuals to pack five years of 529 contributions into a single lump sum to maximize market compounding time.

beschreibung:
A listener named Lauren DMed Nicole with a simple question: what is she doing to make sure her daughter has more money than she did growing up? Today, Nicole answers in full, walking through the exact accounts, strategies, and tax moves she is using to build wealth for her toddler from day one.

Nicole breaks down the three accounts she opened for her daughter (a 529, a custodial Roth IRA, and a custodial brokerage account), why she gifts directly into the 529 for every holiday, and how she is legally paying her daughter through her business to shift income into a lower tax bracket. Tax strategist Karlton Dennis joins with a clip explaining the rules around paying your kids: what counts as reasonable compensation, how the standard deduction plays into it, and why starting a custodial Roth IRA early can turn a few thousand dollars into over a million by retirement.

Nicole also gets into the life insurance decision every parent needs to make. She explains the real difference between term and whole life insurance, why she chose term for her family, and when whole life actually does make sense.
